approval_boundary.approved: The minimum successor repair is implementation-worthy: gate the supervisor direct-file bottom entrypoint on both __name__ == "__main__" and __spec__ is None, then exercise the actual direct-file main -> run_groups -> prepare_graph -> duplicate-shell path with bounded downstream I/O fixtures.
approval_boundary.deferred: A later source/core review, harmless qualification review, external control review, and any production launch review remain mandatory.
approval_boundary.preserved: BF19 source, core, contract, manifest, ledger prefix, launch-stop evidence, timing/resource/attempt limits, and prior reviews remain immutable.

implementation_requirements: Keep the exact existing direct-file launcher command shape and flags; do not introduce python -m, runpy, AST filtering, source rewriting, sys.path changes, or process-global sys.modules/importlib patches.

Exercise actual successor main(), run_groups(), prepare_graph(), GraphImportContext.ensure/execute_all(), and the duplicate supervisor shell. Mock only the documented downstream evidence/full-replay boundary so the test proves the entrypoint and graph path rather than a copied fixture.

Prove the outer direct-file main is entered exactly once, the parent-stage boundary is reached, and a bounded downstream sentinel is observed. Include a deliberate downstream exception and assert __main__, graph facades/callbacks, and registries restore.

Add near misses for a graph shell with __spec__ None, a foreign host object/path/SHA/role, wrong interpreter/flags/argv, an unregistered dynamic selector, and any route-bypass attempt. They must remain fail-closed.
If symmetric guards are added, test direct-file execution, named import, and graph-shell execution independently; do not claim the supervisor repair covers those entrypoints without those tests.
limitations: This is design approval only. No successor source was edited or executed, and no replay, qualification, admission, analyzer, build, or launch was performed.
The historical BF19 direct-file failure and its no-attempt boundary are evidence for the design, not proof that a BF20 successor is qualified.
resolved_design_points: The recommended fix is the narrow supervisor20 predicate `if __name__ == "__main__" and __spec__ is None: raise SystemExit(main())`; no route alias or recursive CLI allowance is permitted.

The current bridge intentionally preserves the live host name by source path. Therefore host_supervisor20 may have __name__ == "__main__" while its distinct __spec__ is the synthetic graph spec. Tests must assert distinct module/globals, exact path/SHA, non-null synthetic spec and graph role, rather than require __name__ to equal the role string.

Optional symmetric guards on protocol20, admission20, and bridge15 are acceptable only when those files remain independently direct-file entrypoints and their direct-file/named-import behavior is tested; they are not a reason to alter graph identity or add a package execution mode.
A direct-file qualification result cannot substitute for the durable CLI regression: the failure occurred only when the live __main__ supervisor was composed with its duplicate same-path graph shell.
scope: Read-only independent review of the BF19 CLI host execution repair design. This approves only append-only successor implementation and bounded tests; it does not approve source mutation, admission, qualification, replay, analyzer, build, launch, retry, or release readiness.

static_validation.detail: The design bindings match the current supervisor19 SHA b560bfd25b311cdc705ac7bdcd0fe08c828f45f3bd096126964dd212e4b8e2b5 and bridge14 SHA 90546ba9fe66d94a6131dd4280458f31b9cb753264ec4e2a08ebc4836d0c08d3; protocol19 and admission19 were also parse/compile checked.

The recorded failure is consistent with the source call path: direct-file supervisor is the live __main__ host; bridge _bind_host records that name by exact path; _build_shells makes a distinct same-path module with a non-null synthetic ModuleSpec but inherited __name__ __main__; the unguarded bottom main() recursively re-enters the CLI.

For the approved direct-file argv, __name__ is __main__ and __spec__ is None. A graph-created shell has __spec__ set to its Graph ModuleSpec, so the guard suppresses only the duplicate CLI entrypoint while allowing its complete source body to initialize. Named imports likewise do not satisfy the predicate.

The design keeps host object identity, exact source path/SHA, graph role, spec/loader, route table, and strict dynamic-route failures unchanged. It does not rename shells, collapse same-path roles, patch process-global import machinery, or permit the failing route.
The proposed change is append-only BF20 successor work; BF19 design14/contract21/build11 and all prior evidence remain historical inputs, with no attempt/retry or v0131 fallback.
